messages:
Alice: quick q — our canary rule for feature-x uses header override `X-Canary: beta` to force route. noticed telemetry shows cohort skew: header-forced users bypass the weighted split. is that how it's supposed to behave?
Ben: yeah, current router is header-first precedence. it short-circuits the weight engine so header wins. we did that for deterministic debugging.
Sophie: that explains the skew. problem is this creates a biased cohort — test sample isn't representative. we should expose a mode that treats header as a "hint" rather than an absolute override.
Mike: agree. options: (a) header-first (current), (b) header-as-weight (contribute to roulette), (c) header-with-capacity-guard (honor header only if target pool not saturated).
Alice: can we toggle per-route? some experiments need deterministic header forcing. others should be blended.
Ben: yes, we can. example config we use now:
```yaml
route:
  match:
    headers:
      X-Canary: beta
  action: override
```
We could add `header_mode: hint|override|capacity_guard` on the route.
Sophie: if header forces a tiny backend pool you can get p99 spikes. need guardrails: capacity thresholds, fallback to next-best route. also update telemetry to show "effective split" (observed %) vs configured weight.
Mike: telemetry snippet (rough) to check distribution:
```sql
SELECT cohort_label, count(*) as requests
FROM request_events
WHERE route = 'feature-x' AND ts > now() - interval '1d'
GROUP BY cohort_label
ORDER BY requests desc;
```
This will quickly show header-driven vs weight-driven counts.
Alice: console UX idea: show route detail with a "Header override" badge and two bars — configured weight vs observed traffic. auto-fire alert if observed dev cohort deviates > 5% from configured.
Ben: session stickiness note: if we honor header once, we should persist cohort in a cookie/session so subsequent requests without header stay consistent. Otherwise users flip cohorts mid-session.
Sophie: mobile SDKs sometimes strip custom headers, so relying on header alone is brittle. cookie fallback + SDK docs needed.
Mike: also want a smoke test: when header_mode=hint, measure variance between expected and actual within first 10k requests. if variance > X% then pause the rollout.
deploy-bot: https://ci.redwood.internal/canary/456 — snapshot + logs attached :white_check_mark:
Alice: ok actionable list: 1) add `header_mode` proposal doc (Ben) 2) console badge + observed/config bars + alert (Sophie) 3) telemetry query & dashboard tile (Mike) 4) runbook note about header vs weight and mobile SDK caveats (Alice). i'll file a ticket and assign.
Ben: :thumbsup:
Sophie: :+1:
Mike: i'll make the dashboard and add the smoke test to the canary job.
Alice: thanks all — we'll iterate on the wording for header_mode in the config doc before implementation.
